cards.title: Understanding React Rendering
cards.content:
Rendering is the process where React calls your components to determine what the UI should look like. React builds a Virtual DOM and compares it with the previous version to figure out what changes are needed.

function MyComponent() {
  return <h>Hello, World!</h>;
}

cards.title: React Rendering Phases
cards.content:
React's rendering lifecycle is split into two main phases:

  • Trigger: A render is initiated (initial load or state update).
  • Render: React calls components to calculate UI changes.
  • Commit: React interacts with the DOM to update the actual elements.

cards.title: Conditional Rendering
cards.content:
React allows you to conditionally render UI elements using JavaScript operators like if, &&, and ternary operators (? :).

return (
  <div>
    {isLoggedIn ? <AdminDashboard /> : <LoginForm />}
  </div>
);
